abstract.#text: "A startling account of the meaning of Jesus and the origin of Christianity based on gnostic gospels and other secret texts, written almost 2,000 years ago, recently discovered near Nag Hammadi in Upper Egypt." --

titleInfo.title: Johannine Gospel in gnostic exegesis: Heracleon's commentary on John

mods.tableOfContents: Introduction: -- The Jesus of history and the gnostic Christ -- Significance of "gospels" in gnostic exegesis -- Historical data and theological insight: two points of view -- Exegesis of John in gnostic circles -- How representative in Heracleon? -- 1. Jn 1.1-4 in Gnostic exegesis -- Naassene exegesis -- Peratae exegesis -- Valentinian exegesis -- The theological basis of Valentinian hermeneutics -- Three Valentinian exegeses of Jn 1.3-4 correlated -- 2. The Johannine prologue in Valentinian exegesis -- Clement's attack on Valentinian exegesis -- Irenaeus' attack -- Heracleon on the prologue -- 3. John the Baptist (Jn 1.19-34) in Valentinian exegesis -- Three levels of interpretation -- Heracleon's criticism of non-Valentinian baptism -- The Valentinian sacrament of "apolytrosis" -- 4. The temple (Jn 2) in Valentinian exegesis -- The temple as an image of the eclesia -- Heracleon's criticism of non-Valentinian eucharistic theology -- The Valentinian sacrament of the "bridechamber" -- 5. Two types of conversion (Jn 4) -- The "centurion's so": an image of psychic salvation -- The "Samaritan woman": an image of pneumatic redemption -- Two "standpoints" in relation to the pneumatic "marriage" -- 6.
